thread:
maya_marketing: Quick ask — we need a compact heatmap + sanity sweep for the launch deck/webinar. Goal: latency (p50/p95) vs payload size across two model families + quantized variants. Can runtime run a narrow matrix today so we can include the visual in tomorrow's slides?

tom_runtime: Yep. Can you be specific about models, payload sizes, and quantization targets? Also how long can the job run?

maya_marketing: Prefer these axes: models: rwd-base, rwd-large; quant: fp16, int8; payload tokens: 32, 128, 512; concurrency: 1 and 8. 3 trials each, capture cold-start and warmed (after 20 warmup requests). Keep total runtime < 3h if possible.

sasha_data: Add per-token cost estimate and a simple sample payload for embeddings vs generation (we only need generation for the heatmap but cost helps narrative). I'll plot a 2D heatmap (x=payload, y=model+quant) and overlay p95 numbers.

tom_runtime: Sounds doable. I'll queue a targeted sweep with warmup=20, trials=3, seed=42. Prioritizing int8 cold-starts first. Will include token-level timing and tail latency logs.

maya_marketing: Awesome — also can you attach the raw CSV and one small JSON sample for the marketing engineer to sanity-check outputs? We may call out a warmup caveat in the notes.

tom_runtime: Will do. Example command I'm going to run (internal runner):

```
run_bench --models rwd-base,rwd-large \\
          --quant fp16,int8 \\
          --payloads 32,128,512 \\
          --concurrency 1,8 \\
          --warmup 20 --trials 3 --seed 42 \\
          --capture csv,json --note "marketing-heatmap-219876"
```

This will produce CSVs with columns: model,quant,payload,concurrency,trial,p50,p95,mean,tokens,cost_est_usd.

deploy-bot: Job queued: job_id=run-heatmap-219876-01; estimated duration ~2h 10m; priority=high

sasha_data: Quick quality checklist from my side: 1) confirm same infra (same GPU type) across runs, 2) run with empty cache for cold-starts and with prefix cache for warmed, 3) log any OOM/retries, 4) capture stderr for any kernel fallbacks.

tom_runtime: Confirmed: same GPU pool g4dn-xlarge-sim (dedicated bench nodes), cold runs will flush cache; warmed runs will reuse KV cache. Will record kernel fallback messages.

maya_marketing: If p95 variance > 20% between trials, flag it and we'll either re-run or call it out. Prefer we have both raw and a normalized plot (warm vs cold).

tom_runtime: Noted. I'll add a small stats summary file with variance flags. If variance exceeds threshold I'll post a follow-up thread.

sasha_data: I can take the CSV -> plot pipeline once job finishes. If you can drop a tiny sample JSON of the outputs (1 per model/quant/payload) into the shared drive, I'll validate hallucination/format consistency for the slides.

tom_runtime: Will upload artifacts to s3://redwood-marketing/bench/219876/ and ping here when done. ETA ~2.5h.

maya_marketing: Thank you — calling out that webinar narrators want the heatmap to highlight int8 gains at 128 tokens specifically. If anything unexpected pops, call us before we finalize slides. :eyes:

deploy-bot: Job started: run-heatmap-219876-01 at 2198760120

tom_runtime: small note — for int8 we might see slight p95 jitter at high concurrency; I'll annotate that in the summary.

sasha_data: Cool. I'll prep the plotting notebook and a lightweight markdown explainer so marketing can copy text into slides.

maya_marketing: Perfect. Ping when CSV + sample JSON are up.

tom_runtime: Uploaded partial results (cold int8) for quick glance: s3://redwood-marketing/bench/219876/partial-cold-int8.csv. Full dump expected when job completes.

maya_marketing: Glanced — looks promising. Thanks team.
